units.translation: [In the verse of the interpolator τοῖς τἀμὰ παρβαίνουσι νῦν ὁρκώματα [those who now transgress my oaths], with syncope, unless he wrote παραβαίνουσι [they transgress].]
Triclinius correctly explains τοῖς παρανόμοις ἐκείνοις [those lawless ones]. The old scholiast ineptly took it as transitive

and referred it to the birds, about whom the preceding verses speak, τοῖς παραβήσασι καὶ μετοικίσασιν αὐτούς [those who transgressed and resettled them]. Thus Victorius for μετοικήσασιν [having resettled]
sends the Erinys who punishes late upon transgressors
those who now transgress my oaths
those who transgressed and resettled them
Concerning the turning of the eye
where Athenaeus adds ὡς τοῦ θύννου τῷ σκαιῷ ὀφθαλμῷ οὐ βλέποντος, ὡς Ἀριστοτέλης λέγει [as the tuna does not see with its left eye, as Aristotle says]. See Thes. vol. 6 p. 208.
casting his left eye like a tuna
as the tuna does not see with its left eye, as Aristotle says

since the indicative is required, undoubtedly παρηγγάρευσε [he dispatched by courier] should be written with Bamberger, a verb formed from ἄγγαρος [courier], which in the language of the Persians means a courier or messenger, about which we have spoken in its place. There are no other examples of the compound παραγγαρεύω [to dispatch by courier], but more of the simple ἀγγαρεύω [to dispatch by courier], about which see Thes. vol. 1 p. 228, where also the noun παραγγαρεία [dispatch by courier] is discussed.
having quickly sent word to the infantry army
when a man sent word to me from Troy
and they flashed back and passed the word forward
having sent the beacon-light to the watchposts of Macistus
with new messages of the flame
in a defective verse I added παραγενοῦ [be present], where the chorus invokes the help of Juno.
upright witnesses being present for the dead
I extended this advice to my citizens for the future
to advise, to counsel, to admonish
to advise, to counsel, to admonish
to advise and admonish the one who is faring badly
I want to advise you what is best
being a prophet of these things, I advised you kindly
to pray, as the Latins often used deprecor for simple precor
to pray, as the Latins often used deprecor for simple precor
pray to the local gods with supplications for what your desire is to obtain
now, as I pray to you, father Zeus of the Olympian gods, grant
unless he wrote παραίτιος [being a cause], as in fr. 41 in the words of Venus is τῶν δ᾽ ᾿ ἐγὼ παραίτιος [of these I am the cause].
Fate, my child, is the cause of these things
of these I am the cause
rank summoned rank of the long ship
